6) A complex of kinematic indicators, consisting of jerk, tremor, and acceleration parameters, was identified, which allows diagnosing early stages of cognitive impairments with a sensitivity of 93.4 percent, outperforming standard clinical tests in effectiveness.

The scientific novelty of the research lies in the development of a hybrid neural network architecture (CNN-BiLSTM) for the analysis of dynamic time series of handwriting kinematics, as well as a method for generating synthetic samples based on mathematical modeling of pathological symptoms (tremor and bradykinesia). These samples supplemented the unique experimental database of labeled fine motor signals, formed for the first time, during network training. This approach allows compensating for the deficit of clinical data and achieving high predictive accuracy (AUC 0.96) compared to classical machine learning methods.

First, a sensor device functioning on the basis of inertial measurement units was developed. This device represents an economically efficient and mobile solution, allowing non-invasive mass screening of the population in primary healthcare settings, without requiring special technical training from medical staff.

In all the listed publications, the applicant plays a leading role in problem formulation, conducting research, and preparing the main text of the articles.

In the fourth chapter, classical and deep machine learning methods were implemented and experimentally investigated. The tuning and comparative analysis of SVM, Random Forest, k-NN, and logistic regression algorithms were performed. A comparative study of neural network architectures based on recurrent and Transformer models was conducted: the basic LSTM, LSTM with a soft attention mechanism, and Transformer Encoder. A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM architecture for the analysis of spatiotemporal patterns of biomechanical time series of IMU signals was justified and developed, demonstrating the best results among all investigated approaches. Hyperparameter optimization and model performance evaluation using standardized quality metrics were carried out.

In conclusion, the main results of the research were formulated, scientific and practical conclusions were generalized, and promising directions for further research in the field of applying artificial intelligence methods for the diagnosis of cognitive impairments were determined.

The total volume of the dissertation is 101 pages, including 21 illustrations, 12 tables, and 2 appendices. The list of references consists of 132 publications.
